channel.title: Muhammad Farooq · Writing
channel.description: Essays on retrieval systems, large language models, agents, and the engineering around them.

item.title: OX Alpha: The harness matters more than you think
item.description: I ran the same model inside nine coding harnesses on the same 40 tasks. Scores ranged from 21/40 to 37/40 and token use varied 6x, with nothing changed except the harness. A breakdown of who solved what, where the tokens went, and why minimal harnesses shine on easy work and lose their edge on hard work.

item.title: Qwen3.8-27B reasoning levels are prompt driven, not enforced
item.description: Qwen3.8-27B ships four reasoning effort levels: off, low, medium, and xhigh. They are not enforced budgets, they are sentences in the system prompt. I ran 84 experiments to measure what each level does, what drives thinking length, and how to set them.

item.title: How agent harnesses manage context: cap, slice, search, store
item.description: What occupies an agent's context window and the four moves harnesses use when content does not fit: cap it, slice it, search it, or store it elsewhere.

item.title: Compaction is the hardest problem in agent engineering
item.description: Why agent harnesses summarize old history, what a careless summary destroys, the failure modes that follow, and the patterns that make compaction safe.

item.title: DeepSeek visual primitives: teaching models to reason with a cursor
item.description: Notes on DeepSeek's briefly public paper Thinking with Visual Primitives: boxes, points, and paths placed inside the reasoning trace, and its honest limits.

item.title: DiffusionGemma: what Google's open text diffusion model actually changes
item.description: Notes on DiffusionGemma, Google's first open-weight text diffusion model: how block diffusion refines a 256-token canvas in parallel, the official speed and benchmark numbers, and what it takes to run locally.

item.title: DwarfStar 4: how a 284B model runs on a MacBook
item.description: A 284B parameter model needs 568 GB stored normally. DwarfStar runs it on 128 GB machines at usable speeds. The quantization recipe, SSD streaming, and the numbers.

item.title: How to evaluate an agent harness
item.description: Harness configurations cluster at 74-76% resolve rate while cost varies fourteen times. A five-step method for judging harnesses on accuracy and cost.

item.title: Loop engineering: what it is, when to use it, and when to stay away
item.description: Loop engineering means designing systems that prompt your agents instead of prompting them yourself. What a loop is, what a serious one needs, and the caveats that matter.

item.title: RAG beyond similarity search: how a modern retrieval pipeline works
item.description: Traditional RAG embeds chunks and hopes similarity search finds the right ones. What replaced it: hybrid retrieval, reranking, enrichment, verification, with localGPT as a working example.

item.title: Sub-agents: when one context window is not enough
item.description: Why single-context agents hit a wall, how harnesses isolate work in child agents with the spawn, restrict, collect pattern, and when delegation backfires.

item.title: Tools vs skills vs MCP: how agents acquire capabilities
item.description: Tools are primitives. Skills are knowledge. MCP is neither: a protocol that connects external tool servers to any harness. How the three fit together.

item.title: Harness engineering: why agent performance now lives outside the model
item.description: Same model, same benchmark, six times the performance difference. Two March 2026 papers show the code around the model now matters more than the model. Here is what they found.

item.title: What is an agent harness? The nine components of a great one
item.description: A harness is the fixed architecture that turns a model into an agent. What it is, how it differs from a framework, and the nine components every modern harness needs.
